title: BitGo Adds Bitcoin Staking Through Stacks
summary: BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association (N.A.) (“BitGo Bank & Trust”) is making Bitcoin Staking with Stacks available to institutional clients.
body_markdown:
## **Key Takeaways**


-


BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association (N.A.) (“BitGo Bank & Trust”) is making Bitcoin Staking with Stacks available to institutional clients, who can stake bitcoin directly from their BitGo accounts and earn rewards paid in bitcoin.


-


BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. serves as the qualified custodian for the staked bitcoin, which stays on the Bitcoin network and is timelocked for the length of the bond.


## Earning bitcoin rewards without moving bitcoin


Institutions that hold bitcoin have historically faced a tradeoff when they look for rewards. Most options require the bitcoin to leave its native chain, either by wrapping or bridging it into another network, or by moving custody to a third party that runs the strategy. Others pay rewards in a protocol token, which adds inflation and price exposure to the reward itself.


Fund structures face an additional constraint. An exchange-traded product (ETP) or exchange-traded fund (ETF) issuer generally needs rewards kept apart from principal for accounting purposes. A product that blends the two creates reconciliation work, and sometimes a structural problem.


BitGo is addressing this with a new integration with Stacks. Clients can stake bitcoin held in BitGo Bank & Trust custody and receive rewards in bitcoin, without changing where the BTC principal sits or what it is denominated in. Bitcoin Staking with Stacks pays rewards in BTC. Participation requires locking a paired STX position, and that position carries its own market price exposure.


## How the staking structure works


The integration uses the Stacks PoX-5 protocol, which ties activity on Stacks to bitcoin spent on the Bitcoin network. A position moves through four stages:


-


The client locks bitcoin in a timelocked vault on Bitcoin. The bitcoin remains in BitGo Bank & Trust custody for the full staking period.


-


The client locks a required STX position for a period of time on Stacks, STX being the native token of the Stacks network. The STX position is subject to market price fluctuation.


-


The paired position is registered on the Stacks protocol and becomes eligible for rewards.


-


BitGo claims rewards on the client’s behalf.


## Why qualified custody matters for Bitcoin staking


BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. holds the staked bitcoin as its[qualified custodian](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/qualified-custody-vs-self-custody/) , under the operational and compliance controls that many investment committees and fund mandates require. Clients keep the custody arrangement they already use.


Bitcoin Staking with Stacks was designed so that bitcoin is not lent, bridged, or wrapped. The bitcoin is timelocked using standard Bitcoin script for the length of the bond, and this works for bitcoin held with a[qualified custodian](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/qualified-custody-vs-self-custody/) .


## Reward handling for funds and trusts


Clients can direct rewards to an address that differs from the staking address. For ETP and ETF issuers, this keeps principal and rewards in separate places from the moment rewards are paid, which can help simplify the separation of principal and rewards. Fund issuers should consult their own advisors regarding the regulatory, tax and accounting treatment of staking.


## Availability


The integration is currently limited to whitelisted institutional partners, managed by Stacks Labs. Institutions interested in participating can[get in touch](https://calendly.com/d/crmk-p2t-k78) to express their interest.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does my bitcoin leave BitGo Bank & Trust custody when I stake?


For BitGo Bank & Trust clients, no. The bitcoin is locked in a timelocked vault on the Bitcoin network and remains in BitGo Bank & Trust custody for the full staking period. It is not bridged, wrapped, or moved to another chain.


### What are rewards paid in?


Rewards are paid in bitcoin. They come from bitcoin spent on block production in the Stacks protocol. Rewards are variable, depend on protocol activity and conditions, and are not guaranteed.


### Can I lose principal?


The protocol does not include[slashing](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/how-institutions-can-mitigate-risks-and-maximize-rewards-in-crypto-staking) . However, participation involves other risks, including STX price risk, smart contract and protocol risk, and restricted access to BTC during the bonding period, which could result in delay or loss.


### Who can participate right now?


The launch is limited to whitelisted institutional partners, managed by Stacks Labs.

### Important information


Bitcoin Staking with Stacks is a feature of the Stacks protocol, which is developed and maintained by third parties and is not operated or controlled by BitGo. Staking rewards are variable, depend on Stacks miner activity and protocol conditions, and are not guaranteed; any rates or estimates are illustrative only. Participation requires locking STX, which remains subject to market price fluctuation and may lose value. Staked BTC is subject to a timelock and generally cannot be accessed until the bonding period ends; Although the protocol does not include[slashing](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/how-institutions-can-mitigate-risks-and-maximize-rewards-in-crypto-staking) , participation involves risks, including smart contract, protocol and network risk, which could result in delay or loss.
